links.comparator_used: Covert (undisclosed) therapist AI use, with a no-AI control scenario as reference
links.outcome: Perceived acceptability of AI-assisted psychotherapy and intent to continue treatment
links.effect: Covert use consistently produced the strongest declines in acceptability and continuation intent. Transparent disclosure reduced the penalty but did not eliminate it. All AI-use vignettes were rated lower than the no-AI control (all p<0.001). Older age and greater chatbot familiarity modestly reduced the penalty in transparent conditions.
links.tradeoff: Even with transparent disclosure, ratings stayed below the no-AI scenario, so disclosure only partly offset the negative reaction to AI use.
links.quote: Transparency reduced, but did not eliminate, negative reactions.
